newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mostly lower as cash looks weaker.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mostly lower as cash looks weaker.

text.p: CME lumber futures returned to the weakness of early last week and shrugged off the limit advances late in the week to close mostly lower, traders said.
Lumber ended $7.00 per tbf lower to 0.80 higher with March and May off most. March ended at $406.50 and May at $384.20 per tbf.

Pressure developed from reports that cash trade again turned slow and concerns over the potential of increased lumber supplies from Canada. Canadian mills still have plenty of room under the quota to export wood during the final quarter of the export quota year, they said.

Dealers showed little interest in buying wood after meeting their immediate needs on Thursday and Friday of last week. Business was expected to be light this week as the Canadian Lumberman's Association convention draws people away from the market, they added.
Futures rose the daily limit of $10.00 per tbf in March the last two days of last week and futures started Monday with a $15.00 expanded trading limit. Limits will return to $10.00 on Tuesday.
